description:
Joint causal-SLO-externality P/D placement as TWO co-operating plugin registrations that share one Policy and one shadow table. causal-slo-externality-handler carries ProfileHandler (Pick + ProcessResults) plus PreRequest and ResponseBodyProcessor, and owns the state: the Policy, the per-GPU coefficient table, and the mutex-guarded shadow table of placed requests with its TTL sweeper. causal-slo-externality-picker carries Filter + Picker and runs the argmin over D local plus D*P disaggregated candidates on one signed, unbounded scale. The split is forced by the target's interfaces, not chosen: ProfileHandler.Pick and Picker.Pick share a method name with different signatures (pkg/epp/framework/interface/scheduling/plugins.go:47, :77), so no single Go type satisfies both. It is a Picker rather than a Scorer for two independent reasons verified at this pin: a Scorer returns a per-endpoint map with no way to name a PAIR (plugins.go:71), and every scorer contribution passes through enforceScoreRange, which clamps to [0,1] (pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler_profile.go:212, :364-372), while J is signed and unbounded -- clamping would collapse every candidate with J <= 0 to one score. runPickerPlugin never clamps, so a picker's own objective survives. Filter is required rather than incidental: Picker.Pick receives only []*ScoredEndpoint and no request, so the arriving request's token count and per-endpoint a_p reach the argmin only via a per-endpoint attribute written in the Filter. The single role-blind profile carries no scorers and sees both pools, since all profiles receive the same candidateEndpoints slice (pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler.go:81). ProcessResults splits the picker's two picks into separate profile results with the decode pick alone as primary, because the director turns every endpoint in the primary profile into a routing destination and comma-joins them (pkg/epp/requestcontrol/director.go:486-496); leaving both in the primary profile would dispatch each request to both pods and still return 200s. Forced settings are hard-wired per config.md 9.2: exact prefill overlap, deployable censored N_out estimates, and collocated-prefill pricing. V=8 is kept rather than folded away so the ablation cohort's validity gate can assert score = 8*(externality - ownGood) exactly. Theta is keyed by the pd-infocomm.io/gpu-type POD LABEL and an absent or unmapped value REJECTS the endpoint and counts the rejection rather than defaulting; both H100 and A100 coefficient sets are transcribed into the config so a hand-added A100 decode pod is priced correctly the moment it carries the label. Required counters are implemented for every declared degradation: the D1 rollforward substitution, tokenization unavailable (D8), prefix unobserved, candidate rejected by reason, block-size mismatch, shadow-table size and reaped entries, output lengths folded into the per-class N_out mean (D9, see below), placement local vs disaggregated, and argmin duration -- eleven collectors, a count a test asserts deliberately.

CORE MODIFICATION: cmd/epp/runner/runner.go, 34 insertions and 0 deletions per 'git diff --numstat', purely additive -- one import plus two registration calls with an explanatory comment. No existing line is changed. No extension point can replace it: plugin types reach the config loader only through the process-global fwkplugin.Registry, which this in-tree binary populates in Runner.registerInTreePlugins, and the treatment overlay switches the arm on by NAMING those types. Without the registration the types are unresolvable and the EPP refuses to start. This is the registration the writer prompt requires, not an algorithm change.

The edit is DERIVED FROM THE v0.10.0 RUNNER ON DISK rather than carried over from the v0.9.0-era whole-file snapshot, which does not build at this pin. Two things about it are pin-specific. First, fwkplugin.Register now takes a StabilityLevel. Both types are registered Beta, and that is a deployment decision rather than a stability claim: ValidatePluginStability refuses to start the EPP when any instantiated plugin is Alpha and --allow-experimental-plugins is absent (pkg/epp/framework/interface/plugin/registry.go:107-119), and expressing that flag requires a per-arm scenario field (router.epp.flags.allow-experimental-plugins, rendered as EPP container args at config/charts/routerlib/templates/_deployment.yaml:116-120, read :8, documented values.yaml:29-32) whose omission would prevent the EPP from starting; Beta avoids that dependency and nothing but the startup gate reads the level, so it costs nothing in behaviour. Nothing else reads the level. Second, the picker is registered with RegisterWithPluginDependencies plus a new exported PickerConfigParser, because instantiatePlugins constructs in TOPOLOGICAL order over a plugin DAG (pkg/epp/config/loader/configloader.go:244-250) rather than in config order. Two plugins with no declared dependency both sit at in-degree 0 and their relative order comes from ranging a Go map (pkg/epp/util/utils.go:42-46): measured at this pin, the picker is constructed before the handler in roughly 5 starts out of 6, the handler lookup returns nil, and the EPP crashloops nondeterministically. The pluginRef tag on pickerParameters.HandlerPluginName supplies the DAG edge, and dependencies are constructed first because TopologicalSort reverses its result (pkg/epp/util/utils.go:75-76). Three tests guard this and all three fail with the tag removed.

Two further v0.10.0 API changes are absorbed in the plugin: PreRequest now returns error (all normal states return nil; the one error is a disaggregated pick whose prefill endpoint carries no metadata, where the header cannot be written and the request would otherwise run locally while every counter recorded a disaggregated placement), and EndpointMetadata.NamespacedName is now EndpointMetadata.ID. Every target citation in the package was re-verified against this pin and the drifted line numbers corrected.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THE MODIFICATION. Upstream rewriting registerInTreePlugins or moving registration out of cmd/epp/runner/runner.go would need the two calls re-placed; the file changed by 558 lines between v0.9.0 and v0.10.0, so this is expected rather than unlikely. A change to the Register or RegisterWithPluginDependencies signature, to the pluginRef tag convention read by findPluginDependencies (configloader.go:304-336), or to TopologicalSort's edge direction would each break the ordering guarantee -- the last one silently, which is why the DAG behaviour is asserted through the real loader rather than by reading the sort. CORRECTION (2026-08-28): an earlier revision of this description and of the runner.go comment asserted that --allow-experimental-plugins is not expressible through the scenario overlay. That was wrong -- 12_router-values.yaml.j2 passes the whole router block through, so any chart field is reachable. Alpha is therefore available at the cost of the required overlay field above; Beta remains the deliberate choice.

NEW DECLARED DEGRADATION (D9), found while porting forward and NOT present in the specification's degradation list. The spec requires the per-class N_out running mean to be updated ONLY on requests that actually completed, because a truncated count drags the estimate down. That is not honourable at this pin. The ResponseBodyProcessor signature carries no error or termination state -- upstream records a TODO to add one (pkg/epp/framework/interface/requestcontrol/plugins.go:76-86) -- and the server FORCES a terminal call with EndOfStream true for every request that picked a pod but never completed, from an error, a client disconnect, or a panic (pkg/epp/handlers/server.go:373-379). The flag that separates the two, reqCtx.ResponseComplete, is director-internal and is already set before the hook runs on the normal paths (server.go:537-540, :608-610), so the two calls are identical from inside a plugin. Declining to fold is not the conservative alternative -- it is STRICTLY WORSE. No request can be confirmed complete, so the mean would never update and nHatFor would return its seed of 1 forever; varDecodeInputs then floors every resident's rem at 1, every resident looks one step from completion, cBase and cLocalAfter land within one iteration of each other, varDecodeContribution goes to ~0 across the whole population, the decode-side externality collapses, and the arm degenerates to its own-good term -- the same degeneration as the tau_e2e = 0 trap that Config.validate refuses to start under. Folding truncated counts biases the mechanism; declining to fold disables it. So the fold happens, and a required counter (causal_slo_externality_output_length_folded_total) makes the foldable population visible -- the same treatment D1 gets, because the fallback is acceptable and the silence is the defect. BIAS: an understated N_out makes residents look closer to finishing, so less value is at risk and the externality is UNDER-counted, biasing toward LOCAL -- the same direction as D2b and D2c, and opposite to D1. This reinforces rather than resolves the bundle's position that the net direction across degradations is not known and is not claimed. It is asserted by TestAbortedRequestFoldsATruncatedOutputLength, which pins the deviating behaviour rather than the behaviour the spec wants, so the deviation is recorded where it happens; documented in the package README's Limitations and Observability sections. SHARED-PACKAGE SEAM (added 2026-08-28, after this arm's own review): this package is no longer this arm's alone, and this arm's declared tree is no longer what it authored. Translating the comparator arm (leastttftjoint) extracted an Arm/Objective seam into this package -- arm.go adds the Arm struct, the Objective interface, Eval, focalObjective and the NewHandlerFactory / NewPickerFactory / NewPickerConfigParser constructors, and evalfixture.go adds a shared test fixture -- so both arms are now the SAME Handler, Picker and Policy parameterised by a different Objective, with this arm bound as FocalArm. That is deliberate and is what makes cross-arm identity of the coefficient table, transfer model, engine agreement, signal bindings and shadow-table settings structural rather than maintained: two arms that are one code path cannot drift, whereas two Config types can drift silently with nothing to catch it. Four production files (config.go, handler.go, picker.go, policy.go) changed under the seam; each reduces to a no-op for an objective whose ReadsSLOValueConfig() is true, and behaviour preservation was verified against approved snapshot v4 rather than asserted -- 188 test functions before and after with an identical sorted name list, all passing. WHY files_created IS A 35-PATH UNION rather than this arm's 29 files: it is consumed by restore_baseline and restore_treatment (pipeline/lib/source_toggle.py:17-43), which need the set to REMOVE to reach baseline and LAY DOWN to reach treatment, not the set this arm authored. Because both arms share one Go package and one cmd/epp/runner/runner.go, neither arm's subset compiles alone: declaring only this arm's files left the comparator's 6 files importing a just-deleted package, which failed the gate's own go vet with "no required module provides package .../causalsloexternality". Both manifests therefore declare the identical 35-path union plus runner.go, and for both the declared set equals exactly the git-dirty set, so restore_baseline from either returns the tree to pristine HEAD with nothing stranded in either direction. Both generated trees are 36/36 byte-identical to the checkout and to each other, so materialising them in either order is idempotent. This arm's image consequently carries the comparator's package compiled and registered; only one can be INSTANTIATED per EPP, because exactly one ProfileHandler is permitted across the whole config (pkg/epp/config/loader/configloader.go:382-391), and the treatment overlay selects an arm by naming its two type strings.
